faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium pacemaker enclosure?
faq.a: Grade 23 ELI (ASTM F136) is the standard for surgical implants. Extra-low interstitials (O<=0.13%) improve fracture toughness. Do not substitute industrial TC4.

faq.q: How is a titanium pacemaker enclosure manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium pacemaker enclosure is manufactured using VAR melting; Closed-die hot forging; CNC swiss turning; Thread rolling. Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Grade 2 CP-Ti for titanium pacemaker enclosure?
faq.a: Stainless steel (corrosion risk), carbon steel (rapid rusting), plastic (low strength)

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium pacemaker enclosure?
faq.a: Titanium Pacemaker Enclosure components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium pacemaker enclosure?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Self-tapping threads require no burrs; use thread rolling instead of cutting; Implant surface must be free of iron contamination; use dedicated Ti-alloy tooling. Proper material selection, manufacturing process control, and inspection mitigate these risks.

faq.q: What surface treatments are available for titanium pacemaker enclosure?
faq.a: Common surface treatments include Passivation ASTM F86. These enhance corrosion resistance, wear properties, and aesthetic appearance.
